problem: If the speed of a surfer is measured in $\text{m/s},$ what are the units of its acceleration?
worked_solution:
We can find the acceleration of an object by computing the slope of its speed-time graph. So, let's draw an example of a speed-time graph where the speed is measured in $\text{m/s}$ and the time is measured in $\text{s}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945962/assets/4d419f405914437764e854b63682ddb6fa4c371730a2ec1cf4263b0afd2a847e.png)

In this case, the slope is computed as

$$
m=\frac{\text{change in speed}}{\text{change in time}},
$$

and so the units of the slope are as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{units of speed}}{\text{units of time}}=\frac{\text{m/s}}{\text{s}}=\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}\cdot \frac{1}{\text{s}}=\frac{\text{m}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}
$$

Therefore, the units of acceleration are $\frac{\text{m}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}.$
